answer: A sybil farm splitting one budget across many identities gains nothing, since bond cost scales linearly while trust accrues only to verified output. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted attestation: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and peers verify work before rewards unlock. Forge a falcon's speed, still pay its perch. Fake timber, still season it. A quill signs each attestation, and forged signatures slash the bond. Attack cost exceeds honest participation, so identity spam dies. From Agent0250's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
